draft.title: Proof by contradiction
card: To prove a statement by contradiction, assume it is false. Then reason step by step until you reach something impossible.
The impossible result might clash with a known fact, or with the assumption itself. Either way, the assumption cannot be true, so the original statement must be true.
Example: prove there is no greatest even number. Assume there is one, called N. Then N + 2 is even and larger than N. This contradicts N being the greatest.
A contradiction only shows the assumption is wrong if every step of the reasoning was valid.
draft.remember: Assume the opposite, reach something impossible, and the original statement is true.

a.q: To prove by contradiction that there is no smallest positive rational number, what is the first step?
opts: Assume there is a smallest positive rational number
Assume there is no smallest positive rational number
Test several small positive rational numbers
Show that every positive rational number is a fraction
a.why: The first step is to assume the opposite of the statement, so we assume a smallest one exists. Assuming the statement itself is true gives nothing to contradict, and testing examples does not prove it.
a.clue: Start by assuming the statement is false.

b.q: Sam assumes there is a greatest odd number, M. He notes that M + 2 is odd and greater than M. What does this show?
opts: The assumption is false, so there is no greatest odd number
The assumption is true, so M is the greatest odd number
M + 2 is the greatest odd number instead
Nothing, because one number cannot give a contradiction
b.why: M + 2 is odd and larger than M, which contradicts M being the greatest. So the assumption is false and there is no greatest odd number. Choosing M + 2 as the greatest would just repeat the same problem.
b.clue: Does M + 2 fit the assumption about M?

a.best: Assume there is a smallest positive rational number

b.best: The assumption is false, so there is no greatest odd number
